title: TwinVPN — Infrastructure health and observability integrity
description: Operator view. ADR-0015 O-20: infrastructure MUST expose health and metrics sufficient to operate an SLO, SUBJECT TO O-13 - so everything here is an aggregate and nothing here can identify a Device, an Owner, a peer pair or a Session. The first row is the one that matters most: it watches the observability system for leaks of its own.

panels.title: Observability integrity — does the pipeline itself hold?
Records dropped for carrying a FORBIDDEN attribute
panels.description: MUST BE ZERO. ADR-0015 O-12 makes tunnel plaintext, packet payloads, private key material, pairing secrets and pre-shared material unwritable to ANY log, metric, trace, crash artifact or diagnostic bundle, at any log level, IN ANY BUILD INCLUDING DEBUG BUILDS - and §7 says SECRET-classified fields have NO RENDERING PATH AT ALL, 'the code that would print them does not exist'. A non-zero value means one does. That is a security defect in the emitting service, not a collector tuning problem.

panels.title: Tier-0 events dropped (ring full)
panels.description: ADR-0015 §8: emission is non-blocking into a fixed-size ring with an explicit drop policy and a dropped_events counter SO THAT LOSS IS ITSELF OBSERVABLE. §13 records the cost honestly: an incident whose cause scrolled out is undiagnosable from the bundle, mitigated by the long-retention significant-events ring alongside the short verbose one.

panels.title: Collector export failures
panels.description: A stalled export must never block, delay or fail a packet-path or state-machine operation (ADR-0015 §8). It is shown separately from service health on purpose: §8 warns that a telemetry outage looking like a network outage creates a feedback loop, so the reliability layer must not consume this.

targets.expr: sum by (exporter) (rate(otelcol_exporter_send_failed_spans_total[$__rate_interval])) + sum by (exporter) (rate(otelcol_exporter_send_failed_log_records_total[$__rate_interval])) + sum by (exporter) (rate(otelcol_exporter_send_failed_metric_points_total[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Scrape success per service (liveness proxy)
panels.description: Read this with architecture.md §2.8 in hand: a control-plane OUTAGE IS A SUPPORTED OPERATING MODE. Established Sessions continue (I5); only new pairings, policy changes, revocations and first contact with a never-seen peer degrade. Neither relay being down is a Session teardown either - ADR-0006 §11.5 makes failover a MIGRATING transition (R-10).

panels.title: Readiness vs liveness — the two are different questions
panels.description: A control plane whose database is unreachable is LIVE (restarting will not help) and NOT READY (do not send it traffic). A readiness probe that returns 200 unconditionally is not a readiness probe. twinvpn_ready reflects DEPENDENCY availability; twinvpn_live reflects only that the process's own invariants hold.

panels.title: Live relays per region
panels.description: ADR-0006 §11.1 rule 3 refuses a RelayMap that drops a region with live sessions below 2 ACTIVE relays in >=2 failure_domains, and architecture.md §2.12 calls a cached set of size 1 A DESIGN ERROR. Below 2 here, failover is not possible in that region.

panels.title: Relay throughput, by carriage and address family
panels.description: ADR-0005 §11.4's three carriages: R-UDP (41641 and 443), R-QUIC (UDP/443, QUIC DATAGRAM), R-TLS (TCP/443, TLS 1.3). They are RACED with a staggered start, never tried in sequence after a timeout. A sustained shift toward R-TLS means UDP is being blocked somewhere and NAT.UDP_BLOCKED should be rising in step.

panels.title: Relay shedding, throttling and draining
panels.description: ADR-0005 §11.5: OVERLOAD IS NEVER SILENT (I6). Whenever the relay throttles, sheds or drains it MUST emit RELAY_STATUS{reason_code, retry_after_ms, suggested_alternatives[]} on the affected flow; a relay that drops without a status frame is a defect. Note that this is NOT a DEGRADED entry - docs/reliability.md R6 reserves DEGRADED for measured quality violations.

panels.title: Durable event write rate against the per-TwinNet budget
panels.description: limits.json control_plane.durable_events_per_second_sustained = 1, burst 20 (ADR-0002 §11.6). Over budget the write is REFUSED with CONTROL.EVENT_RATE_EXCEEDED, which bounds log-flooding denial-of-freshness. Aggregate only: there is no per-TwinNet label, because that would be a per-entity index.

panels.title: C2 stream compaction and admission deferral
panels.description: ADR-0002 N-8: a compaction MUST be announced in band and in order as StreamCompacted{up_to_net_seq}; SILENT OMISSION IS PROHIBITED. §11.7 rule 3: an over-limit attach receives CONTROL.ADMISSION_DEFERRED{retry_after_ms} and a TCP reset or silent drop IS PROHIBITED HERE. Both are visible failures by design, which is what makes them chartable at all.
